targetAudience.primary: Designers and evaluators of multi-Agent systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands task orchestration, shared resources and benchmark metrics.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A team can finish the task while hiding duplication, illegal ordering, resource contention or a repaired handoff.

whyNow: A primary benchmark separates four coordination constructs across 897 oracle-validated executable tasks and 11 models, revealing construct-specific behavior.

externalHook.description: A final result is correct even though the path duplicated work, violated a prerequisite and required manual handoff repair.

coreProposition: Multi-Agent reliability is a vector of separately evidenced coordination obligations; aggregate task success cannot establish reliability when a critical allocation, ordering, mutual-exclusion or handoff contract is weak.

originalValue.description: Maps four benchmark constructs to durable runtime contracts and explains why critical weak dimensions must not be averaged away.

readerTakeaway: Report outcome success beside independent allocation, ordering, exclusion and handoff evidence, with task-specific criticality guardrails.

supported: CoCoBench uses 897 oracle-validated executable tasks across four constructs and 11 models.
Team-size, centralized-state and communication experiments show coordination is not one scalar ability.
unsupported: Direct quantitative transfer to enterprise teams
Business correctness from higher coordination scores

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from same-date external research and remains independently useful without first-party projects.

decisionReason: The Research Object supports a distinct, evidence-bounded argument with practical governance value.
